# Amy Castillo — Amy Castillo Consulting

Available for fractional, interim and M&A HR leadership and independent executive investigations, for companies of any size.

## Services

### M&A HR due diligence and integration
Who it is for: CHROs, SVPs of HR, PE sponsors, corporate development teams and CEOs buying, selling or carving out a business.
What you get: HR due diligence; Day 1 readiness; Benefits and payroll stand-up; Retention agreements; Culture integration.

### Fractional and interim HR leadership
Who it is for: Companies of any size that need senior leadership in any area of HR, such as talent, rewards or employee relations. Includes covering a gap between hires.
What you get: A senior HR leader a few days a month; Or full time during a search or reorganization.

### Independent executive investigations
Who it is for: Boards, CEOs and general counsel facing a matter involving a senior leader.
What you get: Discreet, conflict-free investigations; Senior-leader matters up through GM and VP.

## Headline numbers

## Selected results

### Restructuring · Texas Instruments: 20% Headcount reduction, division later profitable
Problem: A money-losing division had to cut headcount by 20%. The usual practice was same-day notice and a walk-out.
Result: No lasting damage among those who stayed; the division restructured and returned to profit, and many impacted employees found new roles inside TI.

### Safety · Epiroc: −68% Lost-time injury frequency
Problem: As VP of HR and SHEQ, I owned a division-wide injury rate that had to come down.
Result: LTIFR down 68% and TRIFR down 45% since 2023, with three injury-free months in 2025.

### M&A · Epiroc: $760M STANLEY Infrastructure acquisition
Problem: Epiroc's $760M STANLEY Infrastructure acquisition (2024) brought in about 1,380 employees with a 60-day Transition Services Agreement.
Result: Payroll and benefits live inside the 60 days; health plans harmonized for 2026.

## HR expertise

- [M&A](https://amycastillohr.com/expertise-mergers-acquisitions): HR due diligence and integration that carry people, pay, benefits and culture safely through a transaction.
- [Employee Relations & Compliance](https://amycastillohr.com/expertise-employee-relations): Fair, consistent people practices, compliance and safety that protect employees and the business.
- [Total Rewards](https://amycastillohr.com/expertise-total-rewards): Compensation, benefits and payroll that are competitive, compliant and tied to performance.
- [Talent Development](https://amycastillohr.com/expertise-talent-development): Leadership programs, succession and talent reviews that build the bench a business needs next.
- [Talent Acquisition](https://amycastillohr.com/expertise-talent-acquisition): Recruiting built as a system: sourcing channels, employer brand, and onboarding that holds on to the people you hire.

## Experience

### Epiroc (2022 – 2026)
Global Surface Division (~$2B, ~2,200 people across the US, Sweden, Canada, China, India, Australia and South Africa).
- Vice President, Human Resources & SHEQ, 2022 – 2026: Strategic HR and Safety, Health, Environment & Quality leader for the division, plus the NASA region and China (~3,000 people). Member of Epiroc's global People & Leadership Council.

### DJO Global (2021)
Three global businesses with employees in the US, Europe and Asia.
- Senior Director, Human Resources, 2021: Strategic HR business leader overseeing strategic and transactional HR, M&A and integration.

### Commercial Metals Company (2015 – 2021)
Central US division: $2.5B, 3,400 people, 80 locations across eight states.
- Division Director, Human Resources, 2016 – 2021: Led a team of 18 with a $2.2M budget; full HR and workforce strategy for the SVP of the central region and four lines of business.
- HR Director, Corporate & Trading Division, 2015 – 2016: Business partner for corporate functions (~1,100 people), supporting the CAO, CIO, CFO and General Counsel. Partnered on the SuccessFactors HRIS, ATS, Compensation and Recruitment rollout.

### Texas Instruments (2000 – 2015)
~$15B revenue, Fortune 200. From HR intern to Senior HR Manager across R&D, manufacturing and global talent development.
- Senior HR Manager, High Performance Analog (R&D), 2013 – 2015: Business partner for two worldwide units ($600M, 400 people) across the US, India, China, Germany and Denmark. Led restructuring, talent review and succession planning; assessed TI China's leadership bench.
- Talent Development Manager, HPA & Power Management, 2010 – 2013: First in a newly created role spanning leadership, organization and high-potential development for two business units totaling 2,400 people. Designed growth strategy sessions for VPs and GMs.
- HR Manager, Worldwide Facilities, 2007 – 2010: Partner to a 750-person organization across seven countries. Hired a 20-person factory start-up team in three months; built servant-leadership programs with an outside consultancy.
- Executive Compensation Analyst, 2005 – 2007: Analyzed competitor executive pay, selected proxy peer groups and recommended executive pay ranges.
- Professional Development Consultant, 2003 – 2005: Designed and facilitated global high-potential leader programs with C-suite mentoring and action learning.
- HR Generalist, Kilby Wafer Fab, 2002 – 2003: Supported a 650-person, 24/7 fabrication facility of engineers, technicians and operators.
- HR Intern, Digital Signal Processing, 2000 – 2002

## About

I'm an HR executive based in Parker, Texas, with 25 years in manufacturing, mining, steel and semiconductors. Most recently I was VP of Human Resources and SHEQ for Epiroc's ~$2B Global Surface Division.

I've supported HR through 7+ acquisitions as part of due diligence and IMO teams, built an HR Center of Excellence from scratch, and modernized payroll, rewards and recruiting. I now work directly with CEOs, CFOs and operating partners who need senior HR judgment without a full-time hire.
